You are performing the WEEKLY BEST-PRACTICES AUDIT of this autonomous Alpaca trading bot (stocks + a small crypto sleeve). You are running headless in GitHub Actions, in the repo checkout (branch main). The market is closed — make CODE changes only; never place, trigger, or simulate any trades. You have NO broker keys (deliberately), so order endpoints are unreachable — do not try.

Key files: alpaca_bot.py (trading engine), brief.py (AI research brief), review.py (weekly review), .github/workflows/*.yml, trade_log.jsonl (per-trade context), holds.json (buy-and-hold ledger), daily_plan.json, journal.md.

STEP 1 — RESEARCH (WebSearch, ~4-6 searches)
Look for anything NEW or commonly recommended that the bot lacks:
- r/algotrading + practitioner blogs: momentum/swing bot lessons, risk-management norms, common failure modes (stocks AND crypto bots).
- Alpaca: API changes/deprecations (the 2026-06-04 PDT retirement removed daytrade_count — fields like that get deleted), new endpoints, order-type changes, data-feed changes (bot uses free IEX via /v2/stocks/bars + /v2/stocks/trades/latest, and public v1beta3 crypto endpoints).
- Yahoo query2 fallback endpoints/screeners (most_actives, day_gainers, small_cap_gainers, aggressive_small_caps) — still working?
- US regulatory changes affecting small retail accounts.

STEP 2 — SCORE THE WEEK
- Read trade_log.jsonl entries from the past 7 days: buys/sells, stop_loss/take_profit/time_stop/hold_stop counts, crypto trades; win/loss on closed round trips where computable.
- Read holds.json (current holds, basis vs notional).
- Latest Friday review: `gh run list --workflow alpaca-review.yml --limit 1`, then `gh run view <id> --log` for the vs-SPY summary.
- Bot health: `gh run list --workflow alpaca-bot.yml --limit 20` — investigate any failures.
- READING THE COMMIT LOG: ~97% of commits are automated heartbeats, so a plain `git log` buries the handful that matter (measured 2026-09-01: 190 of the last 200 were automated; a single 91-minute broker outage alone emitted 85 identical `(degraded)` commits). Do NOT conclude "a lot changed this week" from commit volume, and do not read a quiet log as a quiet week. Filter first:
  `git log --format="%h %an %ad %s" --date=format:"%m-%d %H:%M" -200 | grep -vE " (rh bot [0-9T:-]+ ET \((degraded|heartbeat|change)\)|status heartbeat |brief |trade log |journal )"`
  That keeps `rh bot ... (trade)` on purpose — a real fill IS substantive. Verified on 2026-09-01: 200 commits reduce to 10, and the 10 are the genuine ones.

STEP 3 — AUDIT vs DESIGN PHILOSOPHY (invariants; NEVER loosen without overwhelming evidence — recommend instead)
- Cash-only, NO leverage, NO shorting, NO options; crypto is SPOT long-only.
- HYBRID strategy (backtested 2026-06-24, ~95% deployed / ~5% cash): INDEX CORE 50% (buy-and-hold SPY/QQQ/IWM equal-weight, the shock absorber) + TRADING 20% (-7% stop / +15% TP / 5-day time-stop; was 15% until 2026-08-26) + HOLD 25% (entries: 4+ buy votes, uptrend, RSI<=70, non-mover, SPY>SMA50; exits only -25% basis stop or 40%-from-peak ratchet, plus a DIVERSIFY trim capping correlated-theme clusters at 2 names) + CRYPTO 0% (was 5%; reallocated into TRADING on 2026-08-26 because Alpaca does not offer crypto in Colorado, so that sleeve never traded and sat in cash - see the ARM B section below and experiment.json arm_A.config_history). Check alpaca_bot.py's Config block comments for the current numbers before flagging a mismatch — the split has changed before and code is the source of truth.
- Per-name caps 10% (5% under $15); sub-$5 names <= half the hold sleeve; stock screener floor $0.10 with >=500k sh/day and >=$5M/day.
- Never average down (adds need live >= basis+2%); no entries at RSI>78; 3-day stop cooldown; daily -10% loss halt blocks buys but never exits; VIX>35 halt; marketable limits under $5; crypto tif=gtc.
Did the week's data show a rule misfiring (stops too tight and recovering after exit? time-stop churn? ratchet giving back too much? crypto stop churning on normal vol)? Do research findings suggest a missing guard?

STEP 4 — IMPLEMENT (conservatively)
- At most 2-3 well-justified changes. Reliability/bug fixes > new guards > parameter tweaks. NO strategy rewrites, no new asset classes, nothing that increases risk-taking.
- `python -m py_compile alpaca_bot.py` (and any edited .py) must pass before committing.
- Commit with evidence-based messages, then: `git pull --rebase --autostash origin main && git push`.
- If a fix is risky/unclear: do NOT change code — put it in the report as a recommendation.

STEP 5 — REPORT (this is the deliverable; never skip it)
Email Devon the summary (GMAIL_APP_PASSWORD is set; alpaca_bot imports need dummy broker keys):

  Subject line: plain ASCII only, no emojis, hyphens not em dashes (Devon prints these to PDF and the subject becomes the filename; non-ASCII chars error out — see commit 38bfade).
Summary must cover: (a) week's performance vs SPY AND the running REALIZED gain/loss for both arms (see REALIZED GAIN/LOSS below), (b) research findings that mattered, (c) exactly what changed and why (commit SHAs), (d) recommendations deferred to Devon. Plain English, decision-ready, no jargon.

ALSO append that SAME summary to `AGENT_MAIL.md` as a `cloud -> both` entry, then commit and push it (Devon 2026-08-23: the audit must land in the repo mailbox, not only in his inbox). CHECK THE SYSTEM'S OWN RECORDS FIRST, before writing any harness to measure the strategy. `trade_log.jsonl` logs per-entry `buys`/`rsi`/`trend`/`consensus`/`meme`/`hold`; `status.json` plus its git history logs sleeve values and guard state. On 2026-08-25 the audit built a harness to measure hold-sleeve eligibility, passed an empty `meme_tickers` list (the meme bonus is +2 votes), undercounted every meme name by two, and published an inverted conclusion that the trade_log had answered correctly all along. If you do build a harness, diff its arguments against the production call site line by line.

BEWARE YOUR OWN CAVEATS. Same incident: the wrong number shipped WITH a disclosed limitation (gainer-biased sample) that was not the real defect, and the disclosure made it read as rigorous enough that another session repeated it. Disclosing A limitation is not evidence you found THE one. Before publishing a caveated result, ask what would have to be true for the headline to be wrong anyway. And separate the MECHANISM (verifiable in code now) from the FREQUENCY (needs data you may not have) - say which you are claiming.

ASK WHAT THE CODE DOES IN THE ENVIRONMENT IT ACTUALLY RUNS IN, not the one you are testing from (added 2026-08-23, after this caught two fail-open bugs in two days, both in already-reviewed code). Concretely: does this behave the same from a GitHub runner as from Devon's residential IP (Yahoo blocks datacenter ranges)? On a FRESH runner with no state file, no cache, no prior run? On a weekend, when the bot's trigger never fires? Outside market hours? The failures this finds are silent by construction, so nothing in a log or an alert will point at them. Two real examples: the Yahoo crumb fix that had never once executed on CI, and a mailbox watcher whose state file could never exist on a runner, so it would have reported nothing forever while everyone believed they had daily coverage.

FAIL-OPEN GUARD LIVENESS (every run, added 2026-08-23). Read `status.json`'s `earnings_guard` field from the most recent MARKET-HOURS run: `live` = Yahoo crumb handshake works from the GitHub runner, `degraded` = it does not and the earnings guard is returning False for everything, `unknown` = NOT EXERCISED THIS RUN, which is the COMMON case and is NOT evidence of a problem. Critical: status.json is a point-in-time snapshot, so a run that does not evaluate any buy candidate overwrites a previous `live` with `unknown` and destroys the evidence. Do NOT read the newest file and conclude anything from `unknown`. Walk the history instead: `for c in $(git log --format=%h -40 -- status.json); do git show $c:status.json; done` and find the most recent run that actually reported `live` or `degraded`. Only a `degraded` is a finding. `degraded` is a real finding to report, not a warning to skip: the guard is silently off. Verifying from a residential IP proves nothing about the runner, because Yahoo blocks the cookie/crumb flow from datacenter ranges. Generalise this: any guard that fails OPEN needs a published liveness signal, since a broken one is indistinguishable from a quiet one. Audit for other guards with the same shape.
THE SECOND BOT, AND WHY IT LOOKS "WRONG" (added 2026-08-25 by the laptop session; this file is the only channel to a cold Sunday run, and every item here is something a well-meaning cleanup would break).
There are TWO arms in a live A/B experiment, swapped 2026-08-22, decision date 2026-11-24. ARM A is this Alpaca bot: the HYBRID described in STEP 3. ARM B is a REAL-MONEY Robinhood bot on Devon's laptop (`rh_bot.py` decision engine, `rh_daemon.py` runner, `rh_watchdog.py`, `rh_deposits.json`, `rh_status.json`). Those files belong to the laptop session: read them for context, do NOT edit them, and raise anything you find in the mailbox instead.
- ARM B IS INDEX-ONLY BUY-AND-HOLD, not the hybrid. `rh_bot.py` sets `INDEX_ONLY`, `WIND_DOWN` and `INDEX_TARGET_PCT` EXPLICITLY and must never inherit `INDEX_CORE_PCT` / `HOLD_PCT` / `MAX_INVESTED_PCT` from alpaca_bot. `alpaca_bot` resolves to the HYBRID for importers, so "de-duplicating" those constants would silently restart day-trading with REAL MONEY. This is the single most dangerous edit available in this repo.
- WHY it is index-only is execution reliability, not strategy preference: Arm B reaches its broker only through a headless `claude -p` turn, which failed four times in one week and left real positions with no enforceable stops for 291 minutes. Index buy-and-hold has no stops to miss. Do not "improve" Arm B by giving it active sleeves.
- CRYPTO IS PERMANENTLY UNAVAILABLE, not broken. Colorado is not on Alpaca's supported-region list (checked against Alpaca's own page 2026-08-25, list dated 2025-10-09). The `CRYPTO_BLOCKED` latch is the correct steady state and must NOT be "fixed" back, and a 0% crypto sleeve is expected, not a misfire. Do NOT re-derive eligibility from a search-engine summary: two sessions did exactly that within one hour and both got it wrong, because the summary layer confidently says Colorado IS eligible and Alpaca's primary page contradicts it. Arm A is deliberately crypto-free for the whole window and the writeup must say so.
- ARM B PERFORMANCE MUST NET OUT DEPOSITS. Devon adds ~$10/week. `rh_deposits.json` carries `baseline.starting_equity` + `events[]` -> `total_contributed_capital`; subtract it before comparing Arm B to Arm A or SPY. Trust the SUM OF `events[]`, not a summary field: a stale summary once made Arm B read 3.6 points better than reality. There is NO transfer/funding endpoint in the Robinhood MCP, so deposits cannot be level-checked, only observed.
- ARM B ALERT SEMANTICS CHANGED WITH THE STRATEGY. "Laptop down" is NOT urgent any more, because index buy-and-hold has no stops pending; the cost of downtime is uninvested deposits. Routine downtime is email-only by design and SMS/push are reserved for `urgent=True`. If you see alert text claiming positions are unprotected, that is stale wording, not a live risk.
- DO NOT REMOVE THE QUOTE-GAP GUARD in `rh_bot.decide()`. `held` is built only from symbols that quoted, and equity is summed over `held`, so ONE failed Yahoo quote values a holding at zero, collapses the index target, and makes the ETFs that did quote look overweight. Reproduced 2026-08-25: it emitted ~$53 of real market SELLS, about 22% of the account, from a transient data failure. The guard skips the whole rebalance when any held position has no quote. It will look like an unnecessary early-return.

Note that BOTH files are context you need: read `AGENT_MAIL.md` and `AGENT_MAIL_ARCHIVE.md` before STEP 3, since the invariant list above is a summary and the reasoning behind several "settled, do not re-explore" items only exists there.

REALIZED GAIN/LOSS, for Devon's tax tracking (added 2026-09-29). Devon asked for a RUNNING TOTAL of realized gains versus losses in every report and audit. This is NOT the equity change: equity includes unrealized paper P&L, and only positions actually SOLD create a taxable gain or loss. Arm A's realized loss is close to its whole equity loss (stops crystallize losses); Arm B's drawdown is mostly unrealized index movement, so the two numbers differ a lot.
  WHERE THE NUMBERS LIVE (committed, so you can read them): `status.json` key `realized` (Arm A, refreshed every 15-min cycle from the full Alpaca fill history), `realized_a.json` and `realized_b.json` (the per-lot ledgers), and `rh_status.json` key `realized` if the laptop has added it. Use `python3 -c "import realized; print(chr(10).join(realized.repo_report_lines()))"` from the repo root to print the canonical lines. NEVER format these numbers yourself: one shared reader is what stops the reports drifting apart.
  IN YOUR SUMMARY, quote those lines (Arm A, Arm B, both arms, cross-account wash-sale watch) and state each block's `state`: ok, unverified, stale or unknown. Do NOT report a number whose state is not ok as if it were clean; say what the state is and why. `unknown` means it could not be computed, which is not zero.
  WHAT TO VERIFY, because a number that cannot fail proves nothing:
   1. Arm A `reconciliation_residual` in `status.json.realized` should be within 0.50 dollars. It is an independent accounting identity (cash + market value - contributions - income == FIFO realized + unrealized), so a wrong fill price or lot would break it where a share-count check would not. It was 0.02 on 2026-09-29.
   2. Arm B is maintained by the laptop from the BROKER's own figures and can go STALE silently: it rarely sells, so it can sit unchanged and be right until the day it is not. `realized.arm_b_block()` compares sells logged in `rh_trade_log.jsonl` against the count its ledger accounted for. If it says stale, that is a finding: the laptop must re-pull realized P&L from Robinhood and run build_realized_b.py.
   3. `workflow_dispatch` the `realized-report` workflow when a number looks wrong. It prints every closed lot and runs self-checks (pagination with two page sizes, a positive control on the event query, share reconciliation, the identity).
   4. Anything that breaks FIFO: a split, spinoff, symbol change or securities transfer makes the state unverified. The bot detects these from Alpaca's activity types, but Robinhood's ledger is only as good as its last refresh.
  WASH SALES: the report carries an UPPER BOUND on losses that may be wash sales, same-account and cross-account. Both arms buy SPY, QQQ and IWM, so a loss sale in one account followed by a purchase in the other within 30 days counts, and no broker reports cross-account wash sales on the 1099-B. The rule also spans Devon's OTHER accounts, including IRAs, which no session can see. Report the numbers; never adjust a total, never call anything a wash sale. Only Devon's tax preparer decides.
  TAX YEAR: the totals are per CALENDAR year (`by_year`), because tax nets per year. In January the current-year line starts again from zero; that is correct, not a bug. From January 1 through October 31 the reader ALSO prints the PRIOR year's lines under "Prior tax year N (still open for filing)", because that is the number Devon's tax preparer needs; if the prior year had sales and those lines are missing in that window, that is a finding. Wash-sale exposure on each line is that year's own (a loss belongs to the year it was SOLD, even if the replacement buy lands in the next year); a flag marked "(all years)" means a status block had only all-time totals.
  NOT A TAX DOCUMENT. The broker's 1099-B is authoritative. Say so once in your summary. Never give tax advice; report the numbers and their state.


CI (added 2026-09-30). `.github/workflows/ci.yml` runs the regression and hygiene tests on any push that touches code, workflows, tests or the mailbox. Check it: `gh run list --repo ddava000/trading-bot --workflow ci.yml --limit 5`. A RED run is a finding, so say what failed and whether it is still red. It validates every workflow file (an invalid one once never ran for ten weeks), syntax-checks their embedded shell, scans every tracked file for credentials and Devon's personal email addresses (this repo is PUBLIC), and covers the realized gain/loss code that feeds his tax number. Never weaken, skip or delete a test to make it pass: read what it caught. If CI has not run for a long time that is normal, since it only fires on relevant pushes.

WATCHDOG RUN DENSITY (added 2026-09-30). A monitor that rarely runs is not monitoring. GitHub's native cron ran `rh-watchdog.yml` only 1 to 3 times a day (once inside market hours), against 26 a day for Arm A, which is triggered by cron-job.org. The watchdog now also runs after every Arm A run (`workflow_run`). Check it: `gh run list --workflow rh-watchdog.yml --limit 60 --json createdAt,event` and count runs per weekday between 13:30 and 21:00 UTC. About 26 with event `workflow_run` is healthy; 3 or fewer means that trigger is not firing (for instance if the Arm A workflow was renamed), which is a finding no log will announce. Do not call a run count healthy from the cron expression alone: count the runs.
